finding.claim: Address6.href() interpolates an unvalidated number|string port directly into the URL authority, so an attacker-controlled port string can inject a userinfo/host (e.g. '80@evil.com') or HTML if embedded unescaped. Conditional on a consumer forwarding untrusted input as the port.
finding.source: Consumer-supplied optionalPort argument (number | string), e.g. a request-derived string passed to href(port)
finding.sink: Returned URL string `http://[${correctForm()}]${optionalPort}/` (ipv6.ts:1458), which a consumer may pass to a fetcher or embed in HTML

trace.note: undefined check only; no type/range/format validation
string prefixed with ':' with no parsing or escaping
concatenated into authority; href('80@evil.com') yields http://[::1]:80@evil.com/ whose WHATWG host is evil.com

finding.guards_checked: Type signature only (allows string). No port range check, no digits-only check, no escaping. Unlike fromURL() (validates port 0-65535) and link() (escapeHtml on prefix/form/className), href() has no controls. Severity low to medium, conditional on consumer misuse.

finding.claim: Address6.isLinkLocal() only returns true when bits 0-63 are exactly fe80:0:0:0, so fe80::/10 addresses with nonzero bits 10-63 (e.g. fe80:0:0:1::1) return false, while getType() and getScope() classify them as link-local. Logic inconsistency; low practical impact because link-local targets generally need a scope to be reachable.
finding.source: Address6 value under test (e.g. fe80:0:0:1::1), supplied by a consumer
finding.sink: Boolean classification used by consumer trust-boundary / SSRF filters that call isLinkLocal() alone

trace.note: embeddedIPv4 check first (not applicable to fe80::)
compares getBitsBase2(0,64) to exact string fe80:0000:0000:0000
getType() uses isHostInSubnet(fe80::/10) and returns 'Link-local unicast' for the same address

finding.guards_checked: Checked embeddedIPv4 path (not applicable), getType/getScope consistency (inconsistent). No route or authz guard applies in this library. Severity low.
